newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end around record highs after Fed.
newsitem.headline: German shares end around record highs after Fed.

text.p: German blue-chip shares hit new record highs on Wednesday amid a wave of short-covering and some genuine buying after the Federal Reserve's unexpected decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
The 30-share DAX closed the bourse session up 20.52 points, or 0.8 percent, at 2,658.97, sailing past an old record at 2,650.49 and set a new all-time intraday high of 2,659.66.
The IBIS index of all-day electronic trade nudged slightly higher in late dealings, ending at 2,663.10 after touching 2,665.65.

Dealers, who had been broadly expecting a 25-basis point hike in U.S. rates, rushed to cover short positions as trading progressed, correcting a brief slide in prices in early trade on the weaker dollar.
"This really was a surprise for many of us. What we've had here is a knee-jerk reaction," said one Frankfurt dealer.
However dealers said there was still some uncertainty in the market after the U.S. decision and also warned that German shares were beginning to look dangerously overbought at such lofty levels.
"I can see this bull run taking us to 2,670 but then the air is starting to get very thin," a Munich dealer said.
Chemical stocks were at the forefront, continuing a spate of popularity, and other heavyweight stocks such as Daimler-Benz and Siemens also benefited from the buyback.
"People are looking for the solid stocks," said one dealer.
Giant chemical groups BASF AG and Bayer AG dominated with gains of 91 pfennigs to 48.97 and 19 pfennigs to 56.58 marks respectively, both on healthy volumes.
